_about: All the numbers in the difficulty. Edit here, then run: python3 tools/grade/gen.py (writes web/suguru/js/gradew.js and java/src/SuguruGrade.java). Raise fit when the numbers change, so stored games are regraded. Technique numbers: 0 naked single, 1 hidden single, 2 neighbour elimination, 3 naked pair, 4 hidden pair, 5 naked triple, 6 hidden triple, 7 single-number chain, 8 xy chain, 9 mixed chain, 10 single-number what-if, 11 what-if with singles, 12 both ways, 13 what-if with techniques, 14 mixed pair (Suguru only, level 4; added 26 Nov. 2026), 15 mixed triple (Suguru only, unit 14 after the triples; added 28 Nov. 2026), 16 short single-number chain (Suguru: the three-link chain, a method of the single-number chain's unit, priced as the chain; added 28 Nov. 2026), 17 nook (Suguru: a cell that touches all of a region but one cell is that cell's number; a method of neighbour elimination's unit, recognised like it (0.6): the fit could not tell 0.6 from 2.2; added 28 Nov. 2026), 18 XY-Wing and 19 W-Wing (Suguru: the three-cell two-option chain and one mixed chain's shape, methods of their chains' units, priced as those chains; added 28 Nov. 2026).
_recog: Recognition: the pattern's base price per technique (adjusted 18-19 Nov. 2026). The mixed triple (15, 28 Nov. 2026) between the triple and the hidden triple, as the mixed pair sits between the pair and the triple: a guess until times exist. The nook (17, 28 Nov. 2026) as neighbour elimination (0.6): in your 128 games without pencil the fit was 0.469 at 0.6 and 0.475 at 2.2, so the times cannot tell; it was taken as easy, as it is to spot.
_link: Length by method: each link of the reasoning beyond the first costs this much, per technique (chains and what-ifs). On top of len (log2 of the length, for every step). A link in a what-if with techniques asks more than a link in a single-number chain (25 Nov. 2026).
_inner: Techniques inside a what-if: inner x the recognition of the hardest of them. Lowered from 0.6 to 0.25 (Nov. 2026): a short what-if with a pair is easier than a long one with singles (the player's experience), so what is inside the chain must not weigh more than the length.
_vis: How well this particular case hides: vis x (shape + openness + work).
_cap: The highest grade (a safety ceiling). The scale used to go to 9.9; from 20 Nov. 2026 it goes above 10, because the hardest puzzles without pencil otherwise bunched up at the ceiling (uncapped: at most 10.1 with and 12.6 without pencil on 142 test puzzles). Level 9 (Diabolical) covers everything from 9 up.
_spot: Overview: an addition by the number of places to make progress (index = number, 4 and above = the last).
_load: Load: heavy steps beyond the heaviest. Repeats of the same technique count 1/(1 + loadTechRepeat x (k-1)).
_singles: Puzzles with only singles: how narrow the path is. singlesFirst 0 = all steps; singlesNakedW 0 = naked singles do not count extra (Sudoku uses both).
_pencil: Pencil. The grades are derived by gen.py: with pencil = base - (1 - anchor) x diff, without pencil = base + anchor x diff, as you used to play = base. 'base' is the fitted numbers (only memory is not 0), 'diff' is how much harder it is without pencil, and 'anchor' is how large a share of the games the base values are fitted to were played with pencil, per technique (0 = without, 1 = with). Set 20 Nov. 2026 from the player's own words: what-ifs and chains over two-option cells with pencil, triples sometimes (on a long search), the rest without. 'diff' is an educated guess; 'repeat' and 'partial' are prepared but set to 0.

pencil._anchor: Share of the fitted games that were played with pencil, per technique: 0 naked single, 1 hidden single, 2 neighbour, 3 naked pair, 4 hidden pair, 5 naked triple, 6 hidden triple, 7 single-number chain, 8 xy chain, 9 mixed chain, 10-13 what-if, 14 mixed pair, 15 mixed triple, 16 short single-number chain, 17 nook, 18 XY-Wing, 19 W-Wing.
pencil._base: Fitted values (the same for both grades, before the pencil difference). Terms not listed here have base 0.
pencil._diff: How much harder without pencil, per term and technique. mem: w x log2(1 + things in your head); tech: fixed; multi: w x cells with several options left (at most multiCap in both directions); trial: what-if from a cell with 3+ options (0/1); built: w x log2(1 + cells built on earlier eliminations); repeat: saves w x the recognition when the pattern has been used before (0/1); partial: partial triple (0/1). len: w x log2(the length of the whole reasoning) for what-ifs (without pencil the whole chain of assumed numbers must be remembered; with pencil it is not written down either, but easier to follow).
